```{python setup}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

import os
import sys
import math

sys.path.append('.')

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Polygon as MplPolygon, Rectangle

from notes_style import (use_chapter, save, tidy, iso, dim_x,
                         INK, LOADCLR, REACTCLR, DIMCLR,
                         DOMCLR, BDRYCLR, FLUXCLR)

IMGDIR = use_chapter("Poisson1D_Heat")

# ---- the worked example used throughout this page (SI units) ---------------
L     = 0.30     # m      wall thickness
kappa = 1.4      # W/(m K) thermal conductivity of concrete
f0    = 500.0    # W/m^3  heat generated inside the wall (heat of hydration)
h0    = 50.0     # W/m^2  solar heat flux absorbed at the sunlit face
g0    = 20.0     # deg C  interior face temperature
HOTCLR = "#e67e22"   # the sun, and the 1 m x 1 m strip


def arrow(ax, p_from, p_to, color=INK, lw=1.8, ms=13, z=6, style="-|>"):
    ax.annotate("", xy=p_to, xytext=p_from,
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle=style, color=color, lw=lw,
                                mutation_scale=ms, shrinkA=0, shrinkB=0),
                zorder=z)


def graph(ax, xlabel=None, ylabel=None):
    """A plotted function: left and bottom axes only."""
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    for s in ("left", "bottom"):
        ax.spines[s].set_linewidth(0.9)
    if xlabel:
        ax.set_xlabel(xlabel, fontsize=11)
    if ylabel:
        ax.set_ylabel(ylabel, fontsize=11)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=9.5)


def box(ax, x0, x1, y0, y1, fc=DOMCLR, ec=BDRYCLR, lw=1.3, z=1, alpha=1.0):
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x0, y0), x1 - x0, y1 - y0, facecolor=fc,
                           edgecolor=ec, lw=lw, zorder=z, alpha=alpha))


def dirichlet_block(ax, x, y, side, label, w=0.55, hgt=0.9, fs=11):
    """A reservoir that holds a face at a known temperature: u = g."""
    x0 = x if side > 0 else x - w
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x0, y - hgt / 2), w, hgt, facecolor="#dbe7f3",
                           edgecolor=BDRYCLR, lw=1.6, hatch="////", zorder=4))
    ax.text(x0 + w / 2, y + hgt / 2 + 0.08, label, ha="center", va="bottom",
            color=BDRYCLR, fontsize=fs)


def insulation(ax, x, y0, y1, side, w=0.3):
    ax.add_patch(Rectangle((x if side > 0 else x - w, y0), w, y1 - y0,
                           facecolor="#fff3cd", edgecolor="#b8860b", lw=1.0,
                           hatch="xxx", zorder=4))


rng = np.random.default_rng(7)


def sources(ax, fx, x0, x1, y0, y1, fmax, n=90, ms=5.5):
    """Scatter + (source) or - (sink) marks with density proportional to |f|."""
    xs = rng.uniform(x0, x1, 40 * n)
    ys = rng.uniform(y0, y1, 40 * n)
    keep = rng.uniform(0, 1, 40 * n) < np.abs(fx(xs)) / fmax
    xs, ys = xs[keep][:n], ys[keep][:n]
    pos = fx(xs) > 0
    ax.plot(xs[pos], ys[pos], "+", color=LOADCLR, ms=ms, mew=1.3, zorder=3)
    ax.plot(xs[~pos], ys[~pos], "_", color=REACTCLR, ms=ms, mew=1.5, zorder=3)
```

This page and its companion, [1D Poisson III: An Axially Loaded Rod](Poisson1D_Rod.qmd),
read the same model problem — the one-dimensional Poisson equation of Hughes,
*The Finite Element Method*, Chapter 1 — in two different physical settings. The
mathematics is identical on both pages. The physics is not, and it is the physics that
tells you what $f$, $g$, and $h$ *are*, what units they carry, and which way they point.

Hughes states the model problem with every constant set to one:

::: {.derivation}
$$
(\mathrm{S}) \qquad
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Given } f : \bar\Omega \to \RR \text{ and constants } g \text{ and } h,
 \text{ find } u : \bar\Omega \to \RR \text{ such that} \\[2pt]
&\qquad u_{,xx} + f = 0 \quad \text{on } \Omega = \,]0,1[ \\
&\qquad u(1) = g \\
&\qquad -u_{,x}(0) = h
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

Choosing a length of one and a material constant of one hides two things that the
pictures below need, so we put them back: the domain becomes $\Omega = \,]0, L[$, and a
material constant $K$ appears inside the derivative, as in [Class 4](4_Class.qmd):

::: {.derivation}
$$
-\left(K u_{,x}\right)_{,x} = f \quad \text{in } \Omega
\qquad\qquad
u = g \quad \text{on } \Gamma_g
\qquad\qquad
\left(K u_{,x}\right) n = h \quad \text{on } \Gamma_h
$$
:::

On this page $u$ is a **temperature** and $K = \kappa$ is the **thermal conductivity**.
Everything below is in SI units.

## The physical problem

```{python fig_wall}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.2, 4.8))
KW = dict(ang=150.0, k=0.55)
T, D, H = 1.3, 3.0, 3.0          # drawn thickness (x), length (y), height (z)


def P(x, y, z):
    return iso(x, y, z, **KW)


def face(pts, fc, ec=INK, lw=1.2, z=2, alpha=1.0, ls="-"):
    ax.add_patch(MplPolygon([P(*p) for p in pts], closed=True, facecolor=fc,
                            edgecolor=ec, lw=lw, zorder=z, alpha=alpha, ls=ls))


face([(0, 0, 0), (0, D, 0), (0, D, H), (0, 0, H)], "#e9e9e9", z=2)      # sunlit face
face([(0, 0, H), (T, 0, H), (T, D, H), (0, D, H)], "#f4f4f4", z=2)      # top
face([(0, 0, 0), (T, 0, 0), (T, 0, H), (0, 0, H)], "#fbfbfb", z=3)      # front cut

# heat generated inside the concrete, seen on the cut face
fx = lambda x: np.ones_like(x)
xs = rng.uniform(0.08, T - 0.08, 60)
zs = rng.uniform(0.15, H - 0.15, 60)
ax.plot(xs, zs, "+", color=LOADCLR, ms=5, mew=1.2, zorder=4)

# the 1 m x 1 m strip that becomes the 1D model
y0, y1, z0, z1 = 1.05, 1.95, 1.35, 2.25
face([(0, y0, z0), (0, y1, z0), (0, y1, z1), (0, y0, z1)], HOTCLR, ec=HOTCLR,
     z=5, alpha=0.55, lw=1.4)
face([(0, y0, z1), (T, y0, z1), (T, y1, z1), (0, y1, z1)], HOTCLR, ec=HOTCLR,
     z=5, alpha=0.30, lw=1.2, ls="--")
face([(0, y0, z0), (T, y0, z0), (T, y0, z1), (0, y0, z1)], HOTCLR, ec=HOTCLR,
     z=5, alpha=0.20, lw=1.2, ls="--")
sx, sy = P(T, (y0 + y1) / 2, z1)
ax.annotate("a 1 m × 1 m strip\nthrough the thickness\nbecomes the 1D model",
            xy=(sx, sy), xytext=(T + 0.55, H + 1.0), ha="left", va="bottom",
            fontsize=10.5, color="#a0520d",
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="#a0520d", lw=1.0))

# the sun and its absorbed flux
sun = (-3.4, 3.9)
ax.add_patch(plt.Circle(sun, 0.42, color="#f5b301", zorder=5))
for a in np.linspace(0, 2 * math.pi, 12, endpoint=False):
    ax.plot([sun[0] + 0.52 * math.cos(a), sun[0] + 0.78 * math.cos(a)],
            [sun[1] + 0.52 * math.sin(a), sun[1] + 0.78 * math.sin(a)],
            color="#f5b301", lw=1.6, zorder=5)
for yy, zz in ((0.6, 1.0), (1.5, 1.8), (2.4, 2.6), (1.0, 2.7)):
    tx, ty = P(0, yy, zz)
    arrow(ax, (sun[0] + 0.6, sun[1] - 0.5), (tx - 0.05, ty),
          color=HOTCLR, lw=1.4, ms=11)
ax.text(sun[0] - 0.2, sun[1] - 0.95, "sunlit exterior face:\nabsorbed heat flux $h$\n(W/m²)",
        ha="center", va="top", fontsize=10.5, color=HOTCLR)

# the interior face and the room
ax.text(T + 0.35, 0.55, "interior face,\nwall temperature held at\n$g$ = 20 °C",
        ha="left", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5, color=BDRYCLR)

ax.text(T / 2, -0.95, "$f$: heat generated inside\n(hydration, W/m³)",
        ha="center", va="top", fontsize=10.5, color=LOADCLR)

# the coordinate and the thickness
arrow(ax, P(0, 0, 0), (T + 1.0, 0.0), color=INK, lw=1.3, ms=11)
ax.text(T + 1.05, 0.0, "$x$", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=13)
dim_x(ax, 0.0, T, -0.35, "$L$ = 0.30 m", fs=11)

tidy(ax)
ax.set_xlim(-4.5, T + 3.0)
ax.set_ylim(-1.8, 5.2)
fig_wall_path = save(fig, "H_Fig1_Wall.png")
```

![A concrete wall, heated by the sun on its outside face, holding a room at 20 °C on its
inside face, and generating heat internally as it cures.](`{python} fig_wall_path`){#fig-h-wall width=80%}

The wall is long and tall compared with its thickness. Far from its edges, nothing
changes as you move along the wall or up it — temperature varies **only through the
thickness**, in $x$. So cut out a strip with a $1\,\text{m} \times 1\,\text{m}$ face and
follow the temperature along it. Every quantity on this page is **per square meter of
wall face**, which is why fluxes are in W/m² and not W.

Three things act on the strip, and each becomes one piece of the strong form:

| What happens physically | Where | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| Heat is generated inside the concrete as it cures | throughout $\Omega$ | the forcing $f$ |
| The interior face is held at the room's temperature | $x = L$ | a Dirichlet condition $u = g$ |
| The sun pushes a known heat flux into the exterior face | $x = 0$ | a Neumann condition $(\kappa u_{,x})\,n = h$ |

## The one-dimensional domain

```{python fig_domain}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.4, 2.3))
Ld = 6.0
box(ax, 0, Ld, -0.18, 0.18, fc=DOMCLR, ec=BDRYCLR)
ax.text(Ld / 2, 0.36, r"$\Omega$", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=17)
for xv, n, lab in ((0.0, -1, "$x=0$"), (Ld, 1, "$x=L$")):
    ax.plot([xv], [0], "o", color=INK, ms=8, zorder=6)
    ax.text(xv, -0.4, lab, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=11.5)
    arrow(ax, (xv, 0), (xv + 1.1 * n, 0), color=REACTCLR, lw=1.6, ms=12)
    ax.text(xv + 1.25 * n, 0.0, "$n=%+d$" % n, ha="left" if n > 0 else "right",
            va="center", fontsize=12, color=REACTCLR)
ax.text(Ld / 2, -0.95,
        r"$\Omega = \, ]0, L[ \qquad \bar\Omega = [0, L] \qquad "
        r"\Gamma = \{0, L\} = \Gamma_g \cup \Gamma_h$",
        ha="center", va="top", fontsize=13)
tidy(ax)
ax.set_xlim(-2.9, Ld + 2.9)
ax.set_ylim(-1.55, 0.85)
fig_domain_path = save(fig, "H_Fig2_Domain.png")
```

![The domain $\Omega$ is the open interval through the thickness; its boundary $\Gamma$ is
just the two faces, each with an outward unit normal.](`{python} fig_domain_path`){#fig-h-domain width=78%}

::: {.step .notes}
- $\Omega = \,]0, L[$ is the **open** interval — the inside of the wall, faces excluded.
  Hughes writes open intervals with outward-facing brackets.
- $\bar\Omega = [0, L]$ is its **closure** — the wall including its two faces. The
  solution $u$ is defined on $\bar\Omega$, since we need its value *at* the faces.
- $\Gamma = \{0, L\}$ is the **boundary**: in one dimension, just two points.
- The **outward unit normal** $n$ points out of $\Omega$: $n = -1$ at $x = 0$ and
  $n = +1$ at $x = L$. It is only a sign in 1D, but that sign is what decides whether a
  Neumann condition reads $-\kappa u_{,x}(0) = h$ or $+\kappa u_{,x}(L) = h$.
- Each point of $\Gamma$ gets **exactly one** boundary condition:
  $\Gamma = \Gamma_g \cup \Gamma_h$ and $\Gamma_g \cap \Gamma_h = \emptyset$.
:::

## The quantities and their units

| Symbol | Meaning | SI units | This example |
|---|---|---|---|
| $x$ | position through the thickness | m | $0 \le x \le L$ |
| $L$ | wall thickness | m | 0.30 m |
| $u(x)$ | temperature (often written $T$) | °C (or K) | unknown |
| $u_{,x}$ | temperature gradient | °C/m | unknown |
| $\kappa$ | thermal conductivity ($K$ in class) | W/(m·K) | 1.4 W/(m·K), concrete |
| $q(x)$ | heat flux in the $+x$ direction | W/m² | unknown |
| $f(x)$ | heat generated per unit volume | W/m³ | 500 W/m³ |
| $g$ | prescribed face temperature | °C | 20 °C |
| $h$ | prescribed heat flux **into** the wall | W/m² | 50 W/m² |

Temperature *differences* are the same in °C and K, so $\kappa$ can be read as
W/(m·°C) with no conversion.

## Where the differential equation comes from

### Conservation of energy on a thin slice

```{python fig_slice}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.2, 4.4))
Ld = 8.0
# the whole strip, with one slice shaded
box(ax, 0, Ld, 3.2, 3.8)
xa, xb = 4.3, 5.0
box(ax, xa, xb, 3.2, 3.8, fc=HOTCLR, ec=HOTCLR, z=2, alpha=0.6)
ax.text(-0.15, 3.5, "$x=0$", ha="right", va="center", fontsize=11)
ax.text(Ld + 0.15, 3.5, "$x=L$", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=11)

# the slice, enlarged
Z0, Z1, Y0, Y1 = 2.4, 5.9, 0.0, 1.9
ax.plot([xa, Z0], [3.2, Y1], color=HOTCLR, lw=0.9, ls="--")
ax.plot([xb, Z1], [3.2, Y1], color=HOTCLR, lw=0.9, ls="--")
box(ax, Z0, Z1, Y0, Y1, fc="#fde9d6", ec=HOTCLR, lw=1.6, z=1)
fz = lambda x: np.ones_like(x)
sources(ax, fz, Z0 + 0.25, Z1 - 0.25, Y0 + 0.25, Y1 - 0.25, 1.0, n=26, ms=7)
ax.text((Z0 + Z1) / 2, Y0 - 0.12, r"generated: $f\,\Delta x$", ha="center",
        va="top", fontsize=12, color=LOADCLR)

arrow(ax, (Z0 - 1.9, 0.95), (Z0 + 0.05, 0.95), color=FLUXCLR, lw=2.4, ms=16)
ax.text(Z0 - 1.95, 1.15, "in: $q(x)$", ha="left", va="bottom", fontsize=12.5,
        color=FLUXCLR)
arrow(ax, (Z1 - 0.05, 0.95), (Z1 + 1.9, 0.95), color=FLUXCLR, lw=2.4, ms=16)
ax.text(Z1 + 1.95, 1.15, r"out: $q(x+\Delta x)$", ha="right", va="bottom",
        fontsize=12.5, color=FLUXCLR)
ax.text(Z0, -0.12, "$x$", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=12)
ax.text(Z1, -0.12, r"$x+\Delta x$", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=12)
ax.text((Z0 + Z1) / 2, Y1 + 0.1, "face area = 1 m²", ha="center",
        va="bottom", fontsize=10.5, color=DIMCLR)

tidy(ax)
ax.set_xlim(-1.0, Ld + 1.0)
ax.set_ylim(-0.75, 4.0)
fig_slice_path = save(fig, "H_Fig3_Slice.png")
```

![A slice of the strip of thickness $\Delta x$. At steady state, heat in plus heat made
equals heat out.](`{python} fig_slice_path`){#fig-h-slice width=80%}

Let $q(x)$ be the **heat flux** — watts crossing each square meter of a plane at $x$,
counted positive when heat moves toward $+x$. At steady state the slice's temperature is
not changing, so every watt that enters or is made inside it must leave:

::: {.derivation}
$$
\underbrace{q(x)\cdot 1}_{\text{in}}
+ \underbrace{f\,\Delta x \cdot 1}_{\text{generated}}
- \underbrace{q(x+\Delta x)\cdot 1}_{\text{out}} = 0
\qquad\xrightarrow[\;\text{divide by } \Delta x,\; \Delta x \to 0\;]{}\qquad
-q_{,x} + f = 0
$$
:::

::: {.step}
Each term is in watts: W/m² × 1 m² for the fluxes, and W/m³ × (Δx · 1 m²) for the
generation. Read the result as **"the flux grows exactly as fast as heat is being made"**:
$q_{,x} = f$.
:::

### Fourier's law: heat flows downhill

The balance has one equation and two unknowns, $q$ and $u$. The material supplies the
second relation. **Fourier's law** says heat flows from hot to cold, at a rate
proportional to how steeply the temperature falls:

::: {.derivation}
$$
q = -\kappa\, u_{,x}
$$
:::

```{python fig_fourier}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.2, 3.7))
xx = np.linspace(0, 1, 200)
cases = [(lambda x: 32 - 10 * x - 5 * x ** 2, lambda x: -10 - 10 * x, +1,
          r"$u_{,x} < 0 \;\Rightarrow\; q = -\kappa u_{,x} > 0$"),
         (lambda x: 18 + 10 * x + 5 * x ** 2, lambda x: 10 + 10 * x, -1,
          r"$u_{,x} > 0 \;\Rightarrow\; q = -\kappa u_{,x} < 0$")]
for ax, (u, du, sgn, lab) in zip(axes, cases):
    ax.plot(xx, u(xx), color=INK, lw=2.2)
    x0 = 0.45
    s = du(x0)
    tt = np.array([x0 - 0.2, x0 + 0.2])
    ax.plot(tt, u(x0) + s * (tt - x0), color=LOADCLR, lw=1.5, ls="--")
    # slope triangle
    ax.plot([x0, x0 + 0.2, x0 + 0.2], [u(x0), u(x0), u(x0) + 0.2 * s],
            color=LOADCLR, lw=1.1)
    ax.text(x0 + 0.22, u(x0) + 0.1 * s, "slope\n$u_{,x}$", ha="left",
            va="center", fontsize=10.5, color=LOADCLR)
    # the wall, coloured by temperature, with the flux arrow in it
    ext = [0, 1, 5.5, 10.5]
    ax.imshow(u(xx)[None, :], extent=ext, aspect="auto", cmap="coolwarm",
              vmin=16, vmax=34, zorder=0)
    a0, a1 = (0.3, 0.7) if sgn > 0 else (0.7, 0.3)
    arrow(ax, (a0, 7.2), (a1, 7.2), color=INK, lw=2.2, ms=16)
    ax.text(0.5, 10.2, "heat flux $q$", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=10.5)
    ax.set_title(lab, fontsize=12)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 1)
    ax.set_ylim(5.5, 36)
    ax.set_yticks([15, 20, 25, 30, 35])
    graph(ax, "$x$", "temperature $u$ (°C)")
    ax.set_xticks([])
fig.tight_layout(w_pad=3)
fig_fourier_path = save(fig, "H_Fig4_Fourier.png")
```

![Fourier's law. The coloured band is the wall, red where it is hot. Heat flows
downhill on the temperature curve: the minus sign in $q = -\kappa u_{,x}$ makes the flux
point opposite to the slope.](`{python} fig_fourier_path`){#fig-h-fourier width=92%}

Substituting Fourier's law into the balance gives the differential equation of the
strong form, in all three of the notations you will meet:

::: {.derivation}
$$
-\left(\kappa\,u_{,x}\right)_{,x} = f
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\left(\kappa\,u_{,x}\right)_{,x} + f = 0
\quad\xrightarrow{\;\kappa \text{ constant}\;}\quad
\kappa\, u_{,xx} + f = 0
\quad\xrightarrow{\;\kappa = 1\;}\quad
u_{,xx} + f = 0 \;\;\text{(Hughes)}
$$
:::

### What the equation says about the shape of $u$

With $\kappa$ constant, $u_{,xx} = -f/\kappa$: **the forcing sets the curvature of the
temperature profile**, point by point.

```{python fig_curvature}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.3))
xx = np.linspace(0, L, 200)
uL, uR = 30.0, 20.0
for fv, col, lab in ((+500, LOADCLR, "$f = +500$ W/m³ (source): concave down"),
                     (0, INK, "$f = 0$: straight line"),
                     (-500, REACTCLR, "$f = -500$ W/m³ (sink): concave up")):
    u = uL + (uR - uL) * xx / L + fv / (2 * kappa) * xx * (L - xx)
    ax.plot(xx, u, color=col, lw=2.2, label=lab)
for xv, uv in ((0, uL), (L, uR)):
    ax.plot([xv], [uv], "o", color=BDRYCLR, ms=8, zorder=5)
ax.text(0.004, uL + 0.7, "$u(0)$ = 30 °C", color=BDRYCLR, fontsize=10.5,
        ha="left", va="bottom")
ax.text(L - 0.004, uR - 0.95, "$u(L)$ = 20 °C", color=BDRYCLR, fontsize=10.5,
        ha="right", va="top")
ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=10.5, loc="upper center",
          bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.2), ncol=1)
ax.set_ylim(18.2, 31.3)
ax.set_xlim(-0.005, L + 0.005)
graph(ax, "$x$ (m)", "$u$ (°C)")
fig_curv_path = save(fig, "H_Fig5_Curvature.png")
```

![Three walls with the same face temperatures and different forcing. With no source the
profile is straight; a source bows it up; a sink bows it down. ($\kappa$ = 1.4 W/(m·K),
$L$ = 0.30 m.)](`{python} fig_curv_path`){#fig-h-curvature width=74%}

::: {.step .notes}
- $f = 0$: $u_{,xx} = 0$, so the profile is a **straight line** and the flux
  $q = -\kappa u_{,x}$ is the same everywhere — what goes in one face comes out the other.
- $f > 0$: $u_{,xx} < 0$, a **hump**. The wall is hotter inside than a straight line
  would predict, because the heat made inside has to flow out through the faces.
- $f < 0$: $u_{,xx} > 0$, a **dip** — heat is being removed inside the wall.
:::

## The forcing function $f$

$f(x)$ is heat **generated per unit volume**, in W/m³. It is the only term in the strong
form that acts in the *interior* of $\Omega$; $g$ and $h$ act only at the faces.
Integrated through the thickness, it gives the heat made behind each square meter of
wall, in W/m²:

::: {.derivation}
$$
\int_0^L f\,dx \quad \left[\tfrac{\text{W}}{\text{m}^3}\cdot\text{m}
= \tfrac{\text{W}}{\text{m}^2}\right]
\qquad\text{e.g.}\qquad 500 \times 0.30 = 150\ \text{W/m}^2
$$
:::

```{python fig_forcing}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(10.0, 4.8),
                         gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[1.0, 1.25]))
xx = np.linspace(0, L, 300)
delta = 0.04
fcases = [
    ("uniform: heat of hydration",
     lambda x: 500 * np.ones_like(x), 500),
    ("absorbed radiation, decaying\nfrom the sunlit face",
     lambda x: 2000 * np.exp(-x / delta), 2000),
    ("cooling pipe at mid-thickness\n(a heat sink, $f<0$)",
     lambda x: -1500 * np.exp(-((x - L / 2) / 0.025) ** 2), 1500),
]
for j, (title, fx, fmax) in enumerate(fcases):
    ax = axes[0, j]
    box(ax, 0, L, 0, 0.12, fc="#f4f4f4", ec=INK, lw=1.2)
    sources(ax, fx, 0.003, L - 0.003, 0.006, 0.114, fmax, n=70, ms=6)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.01, L + 0.01)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.01, 0.13)
    ax.axis("off")
    ax = axes[1, j]
    fv = fx(xx)
    ax.fill_between(xx, 0, fv, where=fv >= 0, color=LOADCLR, alpha=0.25, lw=0)
    ax.fill_between(xx, 0, fv, where=fv < 0, color=REACTCLR, alpha=0.25, lw=0)
    ax.plot(xx, fv, color=LOADCLR if fmax and fv.mean() >= 0 else REACTCLR,
            lw=2.0)
    ax.axhline(0, color=DIMCLR, lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.01, L + 0.01)
    graph(ax, "$x$ (m)", "$f$ (W/m³)" if j == 0 else None)
fig.tight_layout(h_pad=0.6, w_pad=1.6)
fig_forcing_path = save(fig, "H_Fig6_Forcing.png")
```

![Three forcing functions. Top: the wall with a $+$ mark for heat made and a $-$ mark for
heat removed, at a density proportional to $|f|$. Bottom: the same $f(x)$ as a graph.
](`{python} fig_forcing_path`){#fig-h-forcing width=96%}

::: {.step .notes}
- **Heat of hydration** — cement releases heat as it cures, nearly uniformly through a
  freshly cast wall. This is the $f$ used in the example on this page.
- **Absorbed radiation** — sunlight that penetrates a (semi-)transparent layer is
  absorbed over a short depth $\delta$, so $f = f_0 e^{-x/\delta}$ is concentrated near
  the sunlit face.
- **Embedded heating or cooling** — electric heating cables in the slab give $f > 0$
  where they run; a chilled-water pipe removes heat, $f < 0$.
- $f = 0$ is the everyday case of an ordinary, inert wall.
:::

## Boundary conditions

Each face gets exactly one condition: either its **temperature** is known, or the **heat
flux through it** is known. Never both — and, as we will see, never *neither*.

### Dirichlet: $u = g$ on $\Gamma_g$ — the temperature is known

```{python fig_dirichlet}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 3.7))
xx = np.linspace(0, L, 200)
for s, a in ((-60, 0.9), (-20, 0.9), (40, 0.9), (0, 0.9)):
    u = g0 + s * (xx - L) - 180 * (xx - L) ** 2 * (1 if s <= 0 else -0.5)
    ax.plot(xx, u, color=INK if s == 0 else "0.55", lw=2.2 if s == 0 else 1.3,
            ls="-" if s == 0 else "--")
ax.plot([L], [g0], "o", color=BDRYCLR, ms=10, zorder=6)
ax.add_patch(Rectangle((L, 5), 0.04, 30, facecolor="#dbe7f3",
                       edgecolor=BDRYCLR, lw=1.6, hatch="////", zorder=4))
ax.text(L + 0.02, 36, "room temperature\n(a large\nreservoir)", ha="center",
        va="bottom", fontsize=10, color=BDRYCLR)
ax.annotate("$u(L) = g$ = 20 °C", xy=(L, g0), xytext=(0.17, 9),
            fontsize=12, color=BDRYCLR,
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=BDRYCLR, lw=1.2))
ax.set_xlim(0, L + 0.045)
ax.set_ylim(5, 45)
graph(ax, "$x$ (m)", "$u$ (°C)")
fig_dir_path = save(fig, "H_Fig7_Dirichlet.png")
```

![A Dirichlet condition pins the *value* of $u$ at a face. Every one of these curves
satisfies $u(L) = 20$ °C; the condition says nothing about the slope, which is left for
the rest of the problem to decide.](`{python} fig_dir_path`){#fig-h-dirichlet width=72%}

::: {.step .notes}
- $g$ is a **temperature**, in °C.
- Physically: the face touches something so large, or so well mixed, that the wall
  cannot change its temperature — and for the moment can be thought of as room air under a thermostat, an ice bath at 0 °C,
  flowing water, deep ground.
- It is called an **essential** boundary condition: it is imposed directly on the
  unknown $u$. Later, in the weak form, it is built into the trial space $\mathcal{S}$
  rather than appearing in any integral.
:::

### Neumann: $(\kappa u_{,x})\,n = h$ on $\Gamma_h$ — the heat flux is known

Here is the one relation that looks mysterious until you draw it. Start from Fourier's
law: $q$ is the flux toward $+x$, so $q\,n$ is the flux leaving through a face (outward
normal), and $-q\,n$ is the flux **entering** through it. The Neumann condition fixes
the flux entering:

::: {.derivation}
$$
h = -q\,n = -\left(-\kappa u_{,x}\right) n = \left(\kappa\,u_{,x}\right) n
$$
:::

So $(\kappa u_{,x})\,n = h$ is not a new law; it is Fourier's law evaluated at a face,
with $h$ read as **heat flux into the wall**, in W/m². Now substitute the two possible
normals:

::: {.derivation}
$$
\text{at } x = 0 \;(n = -1): \quad -\kappa\,u_{,x}(0) = h
\qquad\qquad
\text{at } x = L \;(n = +1): \quad +\kappa\,u_{,x}(L) = h
$$
:::

```{python fig_neumann}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(10.4, 5.8))
W = 2.2                       # drawn depth of wall shown inside the panel
titles = ["$h > 0$: heat flows in", "$h = 0$: insulated",
          "$h < 0$: heat flows out"]
for i, side in enumerate(("left", "right")):
    n = -1 if side == "left" else +1
    for j, hs in enumerate((+1, 0, -1)):
        ax = axes[i, j]
        # wall occupies the region on the interior side of the face at x = 0
        inside = +1 if side == "left" else -1
        box(ax, 0, inside * W, -1.25, 1.95, fc=DOMCLR, ec="none", z=0)
        ax.plot([0, 0], [-1.25, 1.95], color=BDRYCLR, lw=2.4, zorder=3)
        ax.text(inside * W / 2, 1.8, "wall", ha="center", va="top",
                fontsize=10, color=BDRYCLR)
        ax.text(-inside * 0.9, 1.8, "outside", ha="center", va="top",
                fontsize=10, color=DIMCLR)
        # the temperature near the face: slope = h / (kappa n)
        slope = hs * n * 0.5
        xs = np.linspace(0, inside * W, 50)
        us = 0.55 + slope * xs - 0.05 * xs ** 2
        ax.plot(xs, us, color=INK, lw=2.2, zorder=4)
        tt = np.array([0, inside * 1.4])
        ax.plot(tt, 0.55 + slope * tt, color=LOADCLR, lw=1.3, ls="--", zorder=4)
        ax.text(inside * 1.45, 0.55 + slope * inside * 1.4,
                "  tangent  " if hs == 0 else "", fontsize=9, color=LOADCLR,
                ha="left" if inside > 0 else "right", va="center")
        ax.plot([0], [0.55], "o", color=INK, ms=5, zorder=5)
        ax.text(inside * 0.12, 0.0 + 0.55 + 0.35 * (1 if slope <= 0 else -1) + (0.0),
                "$u$", fontsize=11, ha="left" if inside > 0 else "right")
        # the flux arrow across the face
        yA = -0.8
        if hs == 0:
            insulation(ax, 0, -1.25, 1.95, side=-inside, w=0.35)
        else:
            a_out, a_in = (-inside * 1.3, yA), (inside * 0.9, yA)
            p0, p1 = (a_out, a_in) if hs > 0 else (a_in, a_out)
            arrow(ax, p0, p1, color=FLUXCLR, lw=2.6, ms=16)
            ax.text(-inside * 1.25, yA + 0.2,
                    "heat in" if hs > 0 else "heat out", color=FLUXCLR,
                    fontsize=11, ha="center", va="bottom")
        # the resulting sign of the slope
        if side == "left":
            rel = {1: "< 0", 0: "= 0", -1: "> 0"}[hs]
            eq = r"$-\kappa u_{,x}(0) = h \;\Rightarrow\; u_{,x}(0) %s$" % rel
        else:
            rel = {1: "> 0", 0: "= 0", -1: "< 0"}[hs]
            eq = r"$\kappa u_{,x}(L) = h \;\Rightarrow\; u_{,x}(L) %s$" % rel
        ax.text(0, -1.45, eq, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=11)
        if i == 0:
            ax.set_title(titles[j], fontsize=12, pad=10)
        ax.set_xlim(-2.4, 2.4)
        ax.set_ylim(-2.0, 2.0)
        tidy(ax)
fig.text(0.005, 0.74, "left face\n$x = 0$\n$n = -1$", ha="left", va="center",
         fontsize=11.5)
fig.text(0.005, 0.28, "right face\n$x = L$\n$n = +1$", ha="left", va="center",
         fontsize=11.5)
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.99, wspace=0.08, hspace=0.18)
fig_neu_path = save(fig, "H_Fig8_Neumann.png")
```

![The Neumann condition at either face, for heating, insulation, and cooling. The black
curve is the temperature near the face and the dashed red line is its tangent there.
Whichever face it acts on, heat entering ($h > 0$) makes the face the hot spot, so the
temperature always falls *away from* the face into the wall — which is a negative slope on
the left and a positive slope on the right. That sign flip is exactly the
$n$.](`{python} fig_neu_path`){#fig-h-neumann width=100%}

::: {.step .notes}
- $h$ is a **heat flux**, in W/m², positive when heat goes **in**, on either face.
- $h = 0$ is a perfectly **insulated** (adiabatic) face: the profile arrives with zero
  slope. By symmetry, this is also what the mid-plane of a wall heated equally from both
  sides looks like.
- The **magnitude** of the slope is $|u_{,x}| = |h|/\kappa$. With $h$ = 50 W/m² and
  $\kappa$ = 1.4 W/(m·K), the temperature changes by 35.7 °C per meter — 0.36 °C over the
  first centimeter of the wall. A poorer conductor (smaller $\kappa$) needs a steeper
  gradient to carry the same flux.
- It is called a **natural** boundary condition: in the weak form it will appear on its
  own as the boundary term $w(0)\,h$, rather than being imposed on $u$.
- A real face exchanging heat with air obeys $h = h_c\,(u_\infty - u)$, which mixes the
  value and the slope. That is a Robin condition, and it is not part of Hughes'
  model problem.
:::

### Which face gets which condition

The model problem does not care which face is Dirichlet and which is Neumann — but the
formulas do, through $n$. There are four ways to assign the two faces:

```{python fig_configs}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

xx = np.linspace(0, L, 200)
f = f0
configs = [
    ("(a)  Hughes: $\\Gamma_h = \\{0\\}$, $\\Gamma_g = \\{L\\}$",
     ("h", h0), ("g", g0),
     g0 + h0 / kappa * (L - xx) + f / (2 * kappa) * (L ** 2 - xx ** 2)),
    ("(b)  swapped: $\\Gamma_g = \\{0\\}$, $\\Gamma_h = \\{L\\}$",
     ("g", g0), ("h", h0),
     g0 + (h0 + f * L) / kappa * xx - f / (2 * kappa) * xx ** 2),
    ("(c)  both Dirichlet: $\\Gamma_g = \\{0, L\\}$, $\\Gamma_h = \\emptyset$",
     ("g", 35.0), ("g", g0),
     35.0 + (g0 - 35.0) * xx / L + f / (2 * kappa) * xx * (L - xx)),
    ("(d)  both Neumann: $\\Gamma_h = \\{0, L\\}$, $\\Gamma_g = \\emptyset$",
     ("h", h0), ("h", -(h0 + f * L)), None),
]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(10.0, 11.0),
                         gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1.0, 1.25]))
for i, (title, bcL, bcR, u) in enumerate(configs):
    ax = axes[i, 0]
    box(ax, 0, 3.0, -0.35, 0.35)
    sources(ax, lambda x: np.ones_like(x), 0.1, 2.9, -0.28, 0.28, 1.0, n=18)
    for xv, (kind, val), inside in ((0.0, bcL, +1), (3.0, bcR, -1)):
        if kind == "g":
            dirichlet_block(ax, xv, 0.0, -inside, "$g$ = %.0f °C" % val,
                            w=0.5, hgt=0.9, fs=10.5)
        else:
            a0, a1 = (xv - inside * 1.2, 0.0), (xv - inside * 0.02, 0.0)
            if val < 0:
                a0, a1 = a1, a0
            arrow(ax, a0, a1, color=FLUXCLR, lw=2.4, ms=15)
            ax.text(xv - inside * 0.75, 0.5,
                    ("$h$ = %+.0f\nW/m²" % val).replace("-", "−"),
                    ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5, color=FLUXCLR)
    ax.text(1.5, -0.55, "$f$ = 500 W/m³", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=10,
            color=LOADCLR)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11.5, loc="left")
    tidy(ax)
    ax.set_xlim(-1.5, 4.5)
    ax.set_ylim(-1.1, 1.5)

    ax = axes[i, 1]
    if u is not None:
        ax.plot(xx, u, color=INK, lw=2.2)
        for xv, (kind, val), inside in ((0.0, bcL, +1), (L, bcR, -1)):
            ui = np.interp(xv, xx, u)
            if kind == "g":
                ax.plot([xv], [ui], "o", color=BDRYCLR, ms=8, zorder=5)
            else:
                s = (val / kappa) * (-1 if xv == 0 else 1)
                tt = np.array([xv, xv + inside * 0.09])
                ax.plot(tt, ui + s * (tt - xv), color=FLUXCLR, lw=2.0, ls="--")
    else:
        base = -h0 / kappa * xx - f / (2 * kappa) * xx ** 2
        for c in (35, 45, 55, 65):
            ax.plot(xx, c + base, color=INK if c == 45 else "0.6",
                    lw=2.2 if c == 45 else 1.3, ls="-" if c == 45 else "--")
        ax.text(0.5 * L, 66, "$u + C$ solves it for every constant $C$",
                ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.005, L + 0.005)
    ax.set_ylim(5, 72)
    graph(ax, "$x$ (m)" if i == 3 else None, "$u$ (°C)")
fig.tight_layout(h_pad=1.4, w_pad=2.0)
fig_configs_path = save(fig, "H_Fig9_Configurations.png")
```

![The four ways to assign the two faces, each with the same wall and the same
$f$ = 500 W/m³. On the right, blue dots are Dirichlet values the curve must pass through;
dashed teal lines are the slopes that Neumann data force on it.](`{python} fig_configs_path`){#fig-h-configs width=100%}

::: {.step .notes}
- **(a) Hughes' arrangement.** Flux given at $x = 0$, temperature at $x = L$:
  $\;u(L) = g,\;\; -\kappa u_{,x}(0) = h$.
- **(b) Swapped.** Temperature given at $x = 0$, flux at $x = L$:
  $\;u(0) = g,\;\; +\kappa u_{,x}(L) = h$. Only the sign in front of $\kappa u_{,x}$
  changes. Note that (b) is the *mirror image* of (a), sun on the right instead of the
  left — and $h$ = +50 W/m² in both, because in both the sun pushes heat **in**. The sign
  of the heat-flux $h$ follows the wall, not the $x$-axis.
- **(c) Two Dirichlet faces** is a well-posed problem, with two values
  $g_0 = u(0)$ and $g_L = u(L)$. Hughes' notation then carries a $g$ for each point of
  $\Gamma_g$.
- **(d) Two Neumann faces** is **not** a well-posed problem, for two reasons:
    - *Uniqueness fails.* Flux data only ever see $u_{,x}$, so adding any constant to a
      solution gives another one. The temperature level is never pinned down.
    - *Existence needs luck.* At steady state, every watt in must come out:
      $h_0 + h_L + \int_0^L f\,dx = 0$. The panel uses $h_L$ = −200 W/m² for exactly
      this reason (50 in, 150 made, 200 out). Any other $h_L$ has **no** steady solution
      at all — the wall just keeps heating up or cooling down.
- So **$\Gamma_g$ must not be empty**: at least one face needs a known temperature.
:::

## The strong form, complete

Collecting the pieces, for Hughes' arrangement (a):

::: {.derivation}
$$
(\mathrm{S}) \qquad
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Given } f : \bar\Omega \to \RR \;[\text{W/m}^3],\;
  \kappa > 0 \;[\text{W/(m·K)}],\;
  g \;[{}^\circ\text{C}], \text{ and } h \;[\text{W/m}^2],
  \text{ find } u : \bar\Omega \to \RR \;[{}^\circ\text{C}] \text{ such that} \\[3pt]
&\qquad \left(\kappa\,u_{,x}\right)_{,x} + f = 0
   && \text{on } \Omega = \,]0, L[ && \text{(energy balance + Fourier)} \\
&\qquad u(L) = g && && \text{(Dirichlet: known temperature)} \\
&\qquad -\kappa\,u_{,x}(0) = h && && \text{(Neumann: known inflow)}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

and, for the swapped arrangement (b), replace the last two lines by $u(0) = g$ and
$+\kappa\,u_{,x}(L) = h$.

::: {.step .notes}
- It is called the **strong** form because the differential equation must hold
  **at every point** of $\Omega$. That demands $u_{,xx}$ exist everywhere — a smooth
  solution. A wall made of two materials, with $\kappa$ jumping at an interface, already
  strains this requirement; the weak form relaxes it.
- With constant $\kappa$ and $f$, integrating twice gives the exact solution of (a):
:::

::: {.derivation}
$$
u(x) = g + \frac{h}{\kappa}\,(L - x) + \frac{f}{2\kappa}\,\left(L^2 - x^2\right)
$$
:::

::: {.step}
which, with $L = \kappa = 1$, is the $u(x) = g + (1-x)h + \int_x^1\!\int_0^y f\,dz\,dy$
of [Class 4](4_Class.qmd).
:::

## Worked example

```{python example_numbers}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

xx = np.linspace(0, L, 300)
u_a = lambda x: g0 + h0 / kappa * (L - x) + f0 / (2 * kappa) * (L ** 2 - x ** 2)
q_a = lambda x: h0 + f0 * x                   # q = -kappa u_,x
dudx0 = -h0 / kappa
u0 = u_a(0.0)
qL = q_a(L)
```

The concrete wall of @fig-h-wall: $L$ = 0.30 m, $\kappa$ = 1.4 W/(m·K), curing at
$f$ = 500 W/m³, with $h$ = 50 W/m² of sunlight absorbed at the outside face $x = 0$ and
the inside face $x = L$ held at $g$ = 20 °C. This is arrangement (a).

```{python example_math}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

print(r"""
::: {.derivation}
$$
\begin{aligned}
u(x) &= 20 + \frac{50}{1.4}\,(0.30 - x) + \frac{500}{2(1.4)}\,(0.09 - x^2)
  \quad [{}^\circ\text{C}] \\[4pt]
u(0) &= 20 + %.2f + %.2f = %.1f\ {}^\circ\text{C}
  \qquad\qquad u_{,x}(0) = -\frac{h}{\kappa} = %.1f\ {}^\circ\text{C/m} \\[4pt]
q(x) &= -\kappa\,u_{,x} = 50 + 500\,x \quad [\text{W/m}^2]
  \qquad\qquad q(L) = %.0f\ \text{W/m}^2
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
""" % (h0 * L / kappa, f0 * L ** 2 / (2 * kappa), u0, dudx0, qL))
```

```{python fig_example}

#| output: false

ax.text(0.125, u0 + dudx0 * 0.12 + 0.5,

        ha="left", va="bottom", fontsize=11, color=FLUXCLR)

        va="bottom", fontsize=11, color=FLUXCLR)
ax.text(0.2, 95, r"$+\int_0^L f\,dx$ = 150 W/m²" + "\nmade inside",
        ha="center", va="center", fontsize=10.5, color=LOADCLR)

fig_example_path = save(fig, "H_Fig10_Example.png")
```

![The solution of the worked example. Top: temperature, pinned at the inside face and
leaving the outside face with the slope the sunlight dictates. Bottom: the heat flux
$q = -\kappa u_{,x}$, which grows by exactly the heat made inside the
wall.](`{python} fig_example_path`){#fig-h-example width=80%}

Every line of the strong form can be checked on the picture:

::: {.step .notes}
- **The differential equation.** $\kappa u_{,xx} = -f$: the temperature curve bends
  down everywhere, at the same rate, because $f$ is uniform. Equivalently,
  $q_{,x} = f$ = 500 W/m³: the flux line in the lower panel is straight with slope 500.
- **The Dirichlet condition.** The curve passes through 20 °C at $x = L$.
- **The Neumann condition.** At $x = 0$ the tangent drops 1.79 °C over the first 5 cm,
  a slope of −35.7 °C/m, and $-\kappa u_{,x}(0) = -1.4 \times (-35.7) = 50$ W/m² $= h$.
- **The energy balance.** 50 W/m² in through the sunlit face plus 150 W/m² made inside
  equals the 200 W/m² delivered to the room at $x = L$.
:::

The same wall with the sun on the other side is arrangement (b): $u(0) = 20$ °C,
$+\kappa u_{,x}(L) = 50$ W/m², and $u(x) = g + \frac{h + fL}{\kappa}\,x -
\frac{f}{2\kappa}\,x^2$ — the mirror image of the curve above, with the *same* $h$.
Compare this with the rod, where mirroring the problem flips the sign of $h$.

## Explore the strong form

Move the sliders and watch each line of the strong form act on the solution. The black
curve is the exact $u(x)$. A blue dot marks each Dirichlet face, and the dashed teal
line is the slope that the Neumann condition forces on its face. The band below the
curve is the wall, shaded by temperature, with arrows showing the heat flux
$q = -\kappa u_{,x}$.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof hBC = Inputs.radio(new Map([
  ["(a) Hughes: h at x = 0, g at x = L", "a"],
  ["(b) swapped: g at x = 0, h at x = L", "b"],
  ["(c) g at both faces", "c"]
]), {value: "a", label: "Boundary conditions"})
viewof hF  = Inputs.range([-2000, 2000], {value: 500, step: 50,  label: "f (W/m³)"})
viewof hH  = Inputs.range([-300, 300],   {value: 50,  step: 5,   label: "h (W/m², into wall)"})
viewof hG  = Inputs.range([0, 40],       {value: 20,  step: 1,   label: "g (°C)"})
viewof hG0 = Inputs.range([0, 40],       {value: 35,  step: 1,   label: "g at x = 0 in (c) (°C)"})
viewof hK  = Inputs.range([0.2, 5],      {value: 1.4, step: 0.1, label: "κ (W/(m·K))"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
heat = {
  const L = 0.30, k = hK, f = hF, h = hH, g = hG, g0 = hG0;
  let u, du;
  if (hBC === "a") {
    u  = x => g + h / k * (L - x) + f / (2 * k) * (L * L - x * x);
    du = x => -h / k - f * x / k;
  } else if (hBC === "b") {
    u  = x => g + (h + f * L) / k * x - f / (2 * k) * x * x;
    du = x => (h + f * L) / k - f * x / k;
  } else {
    u  = x => g0 + (g - g0) * x / L + f / (2 * k) * x * (L - x);
    du = x => (g - g0) / L + f * (L - 2 * x) / (2 * k);
  }
  const q = x => -k * du(x);
  const pts = d3.range(121).map(i => { const x = L * i / 120; return {x, u: u(x), q: q(x)}; });
  return {L, k, f, h, g, g0, u, du, q, pts};
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {L, u, du, q, pts} = heat;
  const W = Math.min(width, 760);
  const dirX = hBC === "a" ? [L] : hBC === "b" ? [0] : [0, L];
  const neuX = hBC === "a" ? 0 : hBC === "b" ? L : null;
  const marks = [
    Plot.line(pts, {x: "x", y: "u", stroke: "#1a1a1a", strokeWidth: 2.6}),
    Plot.dot(dirX.map(x => ({x, u: u(x)})), {x: "x", y: "u", r: 6, fill: "#4a7ba7"})
  ];
  if (neuX !== null) {
    const d = (neuX === 0 ? 1 : -1) * 0.08;
    marks.push(Plot.line([{x: neuX, u: u(neuX)}, {x: neuX + d, u: u(neuX) + du(neuX) * d}],
      {x: "x", y: "u", stroke: "#0d9488", strokeWidth: 2.4, strokeDasharray: "7,4"}));
  }
  const top = Plot.plot({
    width: W, height: 300, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {label: "x (m) →", domain: [0, L]},
    y: {label: "↑ temperature u (°C)", grid: true},
    marks
  });

  // the wall, shaded by temperature, with flux arrows
  const segs = pts.slice(0, -1).map((p, i) => ({x1: p.x, x2: pts[i + 1].x, u: p.u}));
  const qmax = d3.max(pts, p => Math.abs(p.q)) || 1;
  const nA = 7, cell = L / nA;
  const arrows = d3.range(nA).map(i => {
    const x = cell * (i + 0.5), len = 0.8 * cell * Math.abs(q(x)) / qmax, s = Math.sign(q(x));
    return {x1: x - s * len / 2, x2: x + s * len / 2, y: 0.5};
  }).filter(a => Math.abs(a.x2 - a.x1) > 1e-4);
  const band = Plot.plot({
    width: W, height: 110, marginLeft: 55,
    x: {label: "x (m) →", domain: [0, L]},
    y: {axis: null, domain: [0, 1]},
    color: {type: "linear", scheme: "RdYlBu", reverse: true, legend: true, label: "u (°C)"},
    marks: [
      Plot.rect(segs, {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", y1: 0, y2: 1, fill: "u", stroke: "u"}),
      Plot.arrow(arrows, {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", y1: "y", y2: "y", stroke: "#1a1a1a",
                          strokeWidth: 2.4, headLength: 10})
    ]
  });
  return html`<div>${top}${band}</div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {L, k, f, h, u, du, q} = heat;
  const fmt = (v, d = 1) => (v < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(v).toFixed(d);
  const inL = q(0), outR = q(L), made = f * L;
  let bc;
  if (hBC === "a") bc = `−κ u,x(0) = −${fmt(k, 1)} × (${fmt(du(0))}) = ${fmt(-k * du(0))} W/m² = h ✓  u(L) = ${fmt(u(L))} °C = g ✓`;
  else if (hBC === "b") bc = `u(0) = ${fmt(u(0))} °C = g ✓  +κ u,x(L) = ${fmt(k, 1)} × ${fmt(du(L))} = ${fmt(k * du(L))} W/m² = h ✓`;
  else bc = `u(0) = ${fmt(u(0))} °C ✓  u(L) = ${fmt(u(L))} °C ✓  (h is not used: Γₕ = ∅)`;
  return html`<div style="font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1.6; margin: 0.4rem 0 1rem 0;">
    <b>Boundary conditions:</b> ${bc}<br>
    <b>Curvature:</b> u,xx = −f/κ = ${fmt(-f / k)} °C/m², everywhere in the wall<br>
    <b>Energy balance</b> (per m² of wall): flux at x = 0 toward +x: ${fmt(inL, 0)} W/m²
    &nbsp;+&nbsp; made inside ∫f dx: ${fmt(made, 0)} W/m²
    &nbsp;=&nbsp; flux at x = L toward +x: ${fmt(outR, 0)} W/m²
  </div>`;
}
```

::: {.step .notes}
- Set $f = 0$: the curve straightens and every flux arrow has the same length.
- In (a), set $h = 0$: the curve arrives at $x = 0$ perfectly flat, as for an insulated
  face.
- Switch between (a) and (b) with the same $h$: the solution mirrors, and $h$ keeps its
  sign, because it is still heat going *in*.
- Halve $\kappa$: the Neumann slope doubles. A worse conductor needs a steeper gradient
  to carry the same flux.
:::
